catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ad-limina-apo: A 1913 entry on the ad limina visits — bishops' pilgrimages to the apostles' tombs in Rome. The entry sets out their law and meaning. Every shepherd must see Peter's successor. A bond of unity, renewed in person. Paul VI renewed the ancient custom. The visits bind the world Church together.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adytum: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on the adytum — the innermost shrine of the ancient temple. Thomas Poole describes its awful secrecy. Only priests might pass the veil. Pagan and Jewish holy places shared the form. The holiest corner of the old religions.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agaunum: This 1913 reference piece on Agaunum — St. Maurice's abbey of the Theban Legion. Henri Leclercq honors the martyr shrine. Fifteen hundred years of prayer guard the pass. Kings endowed its canons richly. The Alps' holiest garrison. Its treasury holds the martyrs' relics.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amphilochius-: This 1913 reference article on Amphilochius of Iconium — the Cappadocian father. Thomas Shahan praises his orthodoxy. He fought the Pneumatomachi heresy. His canons guided the Eastern Church. A bishop of the golden age. His letters survive in the collections. His feast falls in November's end.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: A 1913 entry on the ancient see of Børglum — the Jutland bishopric. Arthur Taylor notes its medieval line. Its bishops ruled the northern parishes. The Lutherans kept the church. A vanished see of Denmark. Its abbey church crowns the hill.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anemurium: A 1913 entry on Anemurium — the Cilician city, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The sea guards its ruined walls. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the southern coast. Its necropolis lines the shore road.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antimensium: This 1913 reference piece on the antimensium — the consecrated altar cloth. Andrew Shipman explains its Eastern use. No liturgy stands without its relics. The bishop signs each cloth. The portable altar of the East. Its folds protect the holy gifts. Its relics link altar to martyr.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arcanum: This 1913 reference article on Arcanum — Leo XIII's encyclical on Christian marriage. Michael O'Riordan explains its teaching. The pope defended the sacrament's dignity. The family is the Church's cradle. The charter of Christian wedlock. Its teaching guides the marriage courts. Its words are quoted to this day.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arcosolium: This 1913 reference piece on the arcosolium — the arched tomb of the catacombs. Maurice Hassett describes its solemn form. The martyrs slept beneath its curve. The frescoes still guard their rest. The catacomb's honored grave. Its arch frames the painted saints.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-atrium: A 1913 entry on the atrium — the forecourt of the ancient basilica. Thomas Poole describes its colonnaded square. The penitents waited in its shade. The cantharus fountain cooled the court. The church's outer paradise. Its pines shade the Roman courts. Its fountain was the cantharus.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-axum: This 1913 reference article on Axum — the holy city of Ethiopia. Thomas Shahan tells its ancient fame. Its obelisks crown the highland town. The Ark is said to rest there. The Rome of the African Church. Its stelae pierce the highland sky.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-belgium: A 1913 entry on Belgium — the little kingdom's church story. Godefroid Kurth traces its Catholic past. The bishops led the nation's schools. The missions knew its zealous sons. A Catholic nation of the north. Its Louvain university is famed. Its missions span the Congo's breadth.
